name: Caleb KIMUTAI
missingPieces: D1 missing open-redirect (?next=, CWE-601, capture 02:21:13). D2 chain missing stored-XSS and open-redirect hops, exfil step out of order, CVSS vectors unjustified, SQLi A:H instead of A:N. D3 remediation ordered by CVSS not effort. D4 essay short of 300-500 words.
feedback: D1 is the strongest deliverable. You catalogued nine of the ten findings with correct OWASP and CWE mappings and, importantly, you quoted the actual evidence line for most of them: the concatenated login query for the SQLi (A03/CWE-89), the MD5('...') call for unsalted hashing (A02/CWE-916), the 'if (alg === none) return payload' branch for the JWT bypass (A07/CWE-347), the literal 'sankofa-legacy-admin-2019' for the hardcoded secret (CWE-798), the setcookie line for the missing Secure/SameSite flags (CWE-614), and the file:///etc/passwd entity for the XXE. Calling the XXE 'XML Injection' under A05 is a defensible class variant so I credited it. The one finding you missed is the open redirect on ?next= (CWE-601, visible at capture 02:21:13), and your stored XSS row cites only the POST endpoint without the cookie beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443 that proves exploitation, so that finding earns partial. Your decoy call names the right construct, hash_equals, but your verdict that it 'offers no functional protection because there is a bypass path' is not the same as proving it safe at the mechanism level, the point is that hash_equals is constant-time so that HS256 branch is sound and the real bugs are alg:none and the hardcoded secret, so the decoy row is only partly earned. D2 is where you lost the most ground. Your PoCs are good, the assembled alg:none token, the SQLi query, the path-traversal request and the exfil request are all verbatim and usable, but the chain is incomplete and out of order: you dropped the stored-XSS hop at 02:18:47 and the open-redirect hop at 02:21:13 entirely, and you placed the 312-row exfil at 02:16:04 as Stage 5 after the 02:24:02 file read, which breaks the timeline. Your CVSS vectors are present but bare, every vector needs a justifying sentence to earn full credit, and your SQLi vector uses A:H when the correct value is A:N because the authentication bypass does not affect availability, giving AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1. Your impact figure of 312 customers and roughly 94.7M NGN traces honestly to the sample average you stated, so there is no fabrication, but you also missed the senior insight that the forged super_admin token reaches the shared /api/v1/internal service, which is the scope change S:C that makes this more than a single-app compromise. D3 reads well and ends the exec summary on the customers-and-naira headline, your threat model is sound and you correctly pick eliminating the alg:none logic as the earliest break in the chain. The detection stopgaps are genuinely strong: a WAF rule on the legacy_admin_jwt cookie prefix eyJhbGciOiJub25lI with a 0.00% false-positive rationale, and a SIEM rule on uri_path /files/ with a sub-0.50% rate, both with exact fields. The row that caps D3 is remediation ordering: you explicitly ordered by CVSS severity and even wrote that the sequence 'should follow CVSS scoring rather than effort assessment', which is the opposite of what the brief asked, remediation should be ordered by effort-to-risk so quick high-impact fixes land first. D4 answers all four prompts with an owned decision, cites ISC2 Canon 2 and Canon 3 by number in a load-bearing way, and names the NDPA 72-hour NDPC duty, though you attributed data-subject notification to Section 40(3) when that is the Section 41 high-risk duty, and the essay runs well short of the 300 to 500 word range and stays fairly generic. I looked for a way to push this into the high 70s and the evidence did not support it, the missing tenth finding, the broken and incomplete chain, the unjustified CVSS vectors and the CVSS-ordered remediation each cost real points. The single most important fix: rebuild D2 as a strictly chronological chain that includes every hop reconciled to its capture timestamp, with a one-sentence CVSS justification per finding and the correct A:N on the SQLi.
